objective: Run the Pi bash tool on just-bash with host passthrough for commands just-bash lacks, TypeScript-first JavaScript-fallback execution, and Billion Context's bash guardrails turned off, as its own module and capability.
scope: Worktree /home/user/holyagent-0.3.1-bash, branch release/0.3.1/feat/just-bash (stacked on release/0.3.1/feat/codex-provider at ce16cb6; the capability registry is in packages/runtime/src/config/capabilities.ts).

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "didn't we agree on using just-bash as the bash tool backend", "we should also support the just-bash's ts/js capabilities (ts as first option, js as fallback)". No earlier record of that choice was found in the original request, the repository, its issues or the Intents.

Decided (maintainer, 2026-11-09, after research showed just-bash 3.6.0 is a simulated shell that cannot run host executables): "use just-bash and allow the executables on PATH and other relevant places (cross-platform)". The Pi bash tool runs on just-bash (through Pi 1.5.0 BashOperations); commands it does not implement resolve to real executables on PATH and other relevant locations, on Linux, macOS and Windows, so git, bun, bunx, mise, gh, node and the holyagent CLI keep working; just-bash TypeScript execution is offered first and JavaScript is the fallback.

Decided (maintainer, verbatim, 2026-11-09): "about the shadowed commands, prefer them instead of the ones in PATH". Where just-bash implements a command itself (rg, grep, sed, find, tar, diff, awk, jq, ls, xargs and the rest), its built-in runs, and the host executable of the same name is not registered; only commands just-bash lacks pass through to the host.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "start the spike", "also, billion context's bash safeguards should be turned off if possible". The just-bash spike starts now. Billion Context tool guardrails on the bash tool (default timeout, output cap, repeat detection) are turned off by HolyAgent where Billion Context offers a setting for it; where it does not, the plan says so.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "everything should be modular and easily upgradeable btw". Each 0.3.1 piece (just-bash backend, host passthrough, TS/JS execution, Codex provider, auto-review, context_management, fff, opencode browse, the screen capability and the capability system) is its own module behind a narrow interface, can be turned off on its own, and every third-party package or binary it uses sits at an exact pin moved only through mise run deps:update, so upgrading one never requires editing the others.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "continue until mergeable or blocked", "btw we shall support both headless use and normal use, that's the point of capabilities, to modularly support systems". Capabilities are the module system: each declares what it needs from the system (a display, a desktop session, a paired browser, a network, an OS) and has a headless and a normal form where both make sense (for example the screen capability uses a headless Playwright Chromium in a cloud or CI session and the paired real browser and desktop computer use on a desktop); setup and doctor detect the system and pick the form, and a capability whose needs are missing is reported, not silently dropped.

Default (root judgement from spike assignment-0mw96w93p-53j2, revisitable): the just-bash backend runs each shell in a Bun Worker so cancel and Pi's timeout terminate it even in a pure shell loop; it mounts an in-memory /usr/bin and /bin of stubs for host passthrough with the shell PATH set to those and the real PATH given to child processes only; it sets defenseInDepth excludeViolationTypes finalization_registry so ReadWriteFs writes work under Bun; it raises the command, loop, work-unit and js timeout limits; it saves cwd and env even when the command runs exit; it offers host-<name> aliases for host programs a built-in shadows; Windows maps a mount per drive. Billion Context guardrails are turned off by setting BILI_GUARDRAIL_BASH_TIMEOUT=0, BILI_GUARDRAIL_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES=0 and BILI_GUARDRAIL_REPETITION=0 for the Pi process.

Read first: the spike report /home/user/holyagent/.git/holyagent/reports/assignment-0mw96w93p-53j2.md (it built and measured this design locally; follow its findings and defaults: a Bun Worker per shell, stub /usr/bin and /bin mounts, defenseInDepth excludeViolationTypes finalization_registry, raised limits, saving cwd and env on exit, host-<name> aliases, a Windows mount per drive) and the Billion Context conflict report /home/user/holyagent/.git/holyagent/reports/assignment-0mw96qjlf-o4zi.md (guardrail settings: BILI_GUARDRAIL_BASH_TIMEOUT=0, BILI_GUARDRAIL_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES=0, BILI_GUARDRAIL_REPETITION=0, passed through the extension environment).
